_comment: Unity 4 shader names found in the shipped build data -> Unity 2022.3 built-in names.
Derived from the 355 Material objects' m_Shader pointers (15 distinct names, 0 unresolved).
Every right-hand side was confirmed by Shader.Find inside the Editor via
unity/Assets/Editor/ShaderProbe.cs -- see README gap 4 for the probe output and for the
two rows that are an approximation rather than an equivalent.
'pending' rows have no confirmed target yet; export_materials.py refuses to guess them.

Mobile-VertexLit-OnlyDirectionalLights: 2022 has no directional-lights-only variant. 100 of 355 materials use this shader, so
roughly 28% of them will additionally receive point lights and shade slightly differently.
A 1:1 result needs a hand-written shader.
Mobile Lightmap Only: The _LightMap slot is dropped because lightmap textures are not imported at all
(LightmapSettings is not migrated). Same for Mobile Lightmap Only2, whose 8 materials

Font: 6 materials, all named 'Font Material'. Their _MainTex points at glyph atlases
(sharedassets0!8/10/12/27, sharedassets14!23, unity default resources!10103) -- one of
which, sharedassets0!27, is among the 3 textures that failed to decode.
IMPACT, measured: only ONE of the six is actually referenced -- sharedassets0!2, by 7
MeshRenderers (level1 and level17 in the shipped scenes, the other 5 in prefabs/bundles).
Those 7 renderers will come in with no material, which shows up as an obviously missing
quad rather than wrong-looking text -- deliberate, because a wrong shader guess here
would give glyph quads with the wrong blend mode, which is much harder to spot.
Unity 2022 regenerates font materials from the Font asset itself, so the real fix is a
Font export step, not a name in this table.
NOTE: an earlier version of this file claimed 'no renderer references them'. That was
wrong -- it came from a single-pass scan that had not finished indexing shaders.
